summary.title: Resign Patterns: Ailments of Unsuitable Project-Disoriented Software
summary.one_liner: A satirical catalog of 22 anti-patterns (named "Resign Patterns") that describe common software project failures, written as a parody of the Gang of Four design patterns.
takeaways: The paper catalogs 22 anti-patterns grouped into cremational, destructural, and misbehavioral categories.
Each entry names a common failure mode, such as legacy code (ProtoTry), two-digit year bugs (Detonator), or tight coupling (ePoxy).
It is a humorous parody of the Gang of Four design patterns book, meant as a warning rather than a guide.
The author notes that patterns in legacy code cannot be extracted because nobody planned to use them.
summary.summary: This short text by Michael Duell, first published in The Software Practitioner in 1997, parodies the Gang of Four design patterns by cataloging "Resign Patterns," which are anti-patterns for poorly run software projects. The patterns are grouped into three sections: cremational (e.g., Abject Poverty, Blinder, ProtoTry), destructural (e.g., Adopter, Detonator, ePoxy), and misbehavioral (e.g., Absolver, Momentum, Eulogy). Each entry gives a name and a tongue-in-cheek description of the symptom and its consequences. The paper is a humorous read with no code or technical implementation details.
